neutral_facts.value: The accused and the victim were neighbours. The victim alleged that the accused harassed her over a period of time, including allegations of rape, emotional blackmail, and threats. The victim initially filed a complaint with the police in 2001, but the charge was initially framed under Section 506(2) of the IPC. The victim did not take any steps for almost 9 years, and the charge under Section 376 IPC was added in 2014. The investigation was complete, and the accused participated in the proceedings. The trial court granted anticipatory bail, which was later cancelled by the High Court. The Supreme Court set aside the High Court's order and restored the trial court's decision to grant anticipatory bail.

key_evidence_accepted.value: The Supreme Court accepted the fact that the charge under Section 376 IPC was added nine years after the initial charge under Section 506(2) IPC, and that the prosecutrix did not take any steps for almost 9 years. The Court also accepted that the investigation was complete and there was no allegation that the appellant may flee the course of justice.

quotes.text: the charge under Section 376 IPC is added only in the year 2014, there is no reason why the appellant should not be given the benefit of anticipatory bail. Merely because the charge under Section 376 IPC, which is a serious charge, is now added, the benefit of anticipatory bail cannot be denied when such a charge is added after a long period of time and inaction of the prosecutrix is also a contributory factor.

witness_credibility.value: The Court assessed the main witnesses, including the prosecutrix, by noting that her statement recorded on 31.05.2001 did not contain allegations of rape, and that the statement was later supplemented by her complaint to Jyoti Sangh. The Court also noted that the prosecutrix did not object to the initial charge under Section 506(2) IPC and that there was no evidence of her trying to influence the witnesses.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the addition of a serious charge under Section 376 IPC should disqualify the appellant from anticipatory bail, and that the delay in framing the charge and the prosecutrix's inaction were factors to consider.

quotes.text: Merely because the charge under Section 376 IPC, which is a serious charge, is now added, the benefit of anticipatory bail cannot be denied when such a charge is added after a long period of time and inaction of the prosecutrix is also a contributory factor.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the addition of the charge under Section 376 IPC after a long period and the prosecutrix's inaction were contributory factors, and that the appellant should not be denied anticipatory bail merely because of the serious charge.

quotes.text: Merely because the charge under Section 376 IPC, which is a serious charge, is now added, the benefit of anticipatory bail cannot be denied when such a charge is added after a long period of time and inaction of the prosecutrix is also a contributory factor.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the grant of anticipatory bail should not be denied merely because a serious charge is added later, and that the court must balance the interests of individual liberty and societal interest.
